summary: The claim that water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius at standard atmospheric pressure is accurate and well-established scientific fact.

claim_analysis.explanation: Pure water is widely known and scientifically established to freeze at 0 degrees Celsius. This temperature serves as a foundational reference point for the Celsius temperature scale.

claim_analysis.claim: This occurs at standard atmospheric pressure.
claim_analysis.explanation: The freezing point of 0 degrees Celsius for water is specifically defined and observed under standard atmospheric pressure (approximately 1 atmosphere or at sea level).

evidence: Pure water freezes at 0°C (32°F) at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure (14.7 psi / 101.3 kPa).
0°C is defined as the freezing point of pure water at standard atmospheric pressure — it's the literal reference point of the Celsius scale.
At standard conditions (1 atmosphere of pressure), the freezing point of water is 0 degrees Celsius (0°C) or 32 degrees Fahrenheit (32°F).
The freezing point of water is 0 degrees Celsius (°C) or 32 degrees Fahrenheit (°F) at standard atmospheric pressure.
The most well-known freezing point is that of water at 32 degrees Fahrenheit or 0 degrees Celsius at atmospheric pressure.
The temperature of the freezing point of water is 32 °F, 0 °C, or 273.15 K. This is the temperature at which liquid water undergoes a phase transition to become solid ice at 1 atmosphere of pressure.
